archetype.name: Better Than Its Record (special-teams sunk)
archetype.definition: A roughly average 5-on-5 team whose bottom-five record comes mostly from a broken penalty kill, below-average goaltending and bad luck in close games, not from being outplayed at even strength.

report.headline: An ordinary 5-on-5 team buried by the league's worst penalty kill
report.take:
The Kings sit 5-8-2, sixth in the Pacific and 29th on the site, and every roster grade is in the D range. Those labels make this look like a bad hockey team. The even-strength numbers say something else: a 49.5 xGF % and 49.0 CF %, both a hair under the league's 50, and 27.9 shots a game, 12th in the league. At five-on-five this is a coin-flip team. It is not getting caved in.

The damage comes from two places. The penalty kill is at 62.5%, dead last and 14.5 points under the league average of 77%. Opponents with any kind of power play have been scoring almost at will. Behind that, the goalies are 29th in Goalies GSAx at -6.5. Most of it belongs to Darcy Kuemper, who has started 10 of 15 games with an .878 save % and -5 GSAx, while Anton Forsberg's .902 in five starts has been closer to serviceable. Add a Pts vs Goal Diff of -2.5 (29th), and the standings are harsher than even a -7 goal differential implies. The power play, at 23.1% and 12th, has quietly been one of the better parts of the team.

The numbers hide a decline that started before this season. Two seasons ago this club posted 105 points with a .552 xGF % and the league's second-best defense. Last season the xGF % slipped to .524, and the 90 points were propped up by a 5.6 Pts vs Goal Diff. Now it is .495. So part of this is real erosion, not just a bad month. The roster shows where: Artemi Panarin (18 points, .607 xGF %), Adrian Kempe and Alex Laferriere tilt the ice, but the middle six of Erik Haula (.354), Trevor Moore (.425) and Scott Laughton (.422) give much of it back. Opposing centers are producing against LA at a rate that ranks 30th.

The direction is better than the record. Over the last 10 the Kings went 5-5-0 with a +3 differential, allowing 3.1 goals a game against 3.47 for the season. A penalty kill this bad almost has to drift back toward normal. That is not the same as being good, though. With the depth forwards losing their minutes and the goaltending a question, a realistic ceiling is the fringe of the wild-card race rather than a return to the 2024-25 team. The current 66-point pace should not hold, but neither should hopes of a quick climb.

strengths.title: Top line drives play
strengths.body: Panarin is the engine, with 18 points, 7 on the power play, and a .607 xGF %. Kempe (.587) and Laferriere (.569) are also comfortably above water. When the top unit is out there, LA out-chances people, and with sound underlying shares that should hold.

strengths.title: Power play and shot volume
strengths.body: The power play converts at 23.1%, 12th and slightly above the league average. Brandt Clarke and Erik Gustafsson add four PP points apiece from the back. The team also generates 27.9 shots a game, so the offense is not starved for volume. It is merely finishing at a below-average 10.8%, which is the kind of number that tends to come up.

strengths.title: Margins improving lately
strengths.body: The last 10 games produced a +3 differential, a full 0.77 goals a game better than the season rate, mostly by allowing fewer goals. Some of the early hole came from an 8-4 opener and a six-game losing streak. The more recent version of the team looks like a .500 club.

concerns.title: A historically bad penalty kill
concerns.body: At 62.5% the kill ranks 32nd of 32 and sits 14.5 points below the league average. It is the single biggest reason a near-even 5-on-5 team has a minus goal differential. Some of it is sample size and some is the goalies, so it should rise, but last season's 74.6% shows this was not a strong unit to begin with.

concerns.title: Kuemper's start in net
concerns.body: Kuemper's .878 save % and -5 GSAx in 10 starts account for most of the team's -6.5 Goalies GSAx, the 29th-best figure. Forsberg's .902 in five starts has been better. A goaltending grade of D- means that, until one of them stabilizes, LA has little margin for its defensive lapses.

concerns.title: Depth forwards and center defense
concerns.body: Haula (.354), Moore (.425) and Laughton (.422) are getting crushed in their minutes. Opposing centers take 42% of the points against LA, against a league norm of 36.6%, and outproduce their own averages at a rate that ranks 30th. Combined with a third straight drop in xGF %, this looks structural, not like bad luck.

trend.note: After a 4-8 October that included a six-game skid, the Kings have gone 5-5-0 over their last 10 with a positive goal differential and fewer goals allowed. The points haven't followed yet: the last five came at the same 40% points rate as the season.

weekAhead.headline: Three home games, two hot goalies and two dangerous power plays
weekAhead.body:
All three games are at home, and none of the opponents is a juggernaut at 5-on-5. Nashville (11th on the site) sits at a 45% CF % and Calgary has a .469 xGF %, so LA should have the puck more often than not. The problem is how the opponents win. Nashville and the Islanders both ride A- goaltending: 6.9 and 8.2 GSAx, with save percentages of .903 and .905. That is a bad matchup for a team already struggling to finish at 10.8%.

The penalty kill decides the week. Nashville's power play runs at 29.8% (4th) and Calgary's at 28.6% (5th), and either can feast on LA's 62.5% kill. The Islanders, at 14.6%, are the one opponent that cannot exploit it. Calgary, 28th in Goal Diff / GP, owns a record propped up by the league's second-best Pts vs Goal Diff and is the most winnable game. Two wins out of three would be a solid week. One is the likelier floor.

keyMatchups.title: LA's kill against Nashville's power play
keyMatchups.body: Nashville converts 29.8% of its chances and also kills 88.5%, so the special-teams battle tilts hard toward the Predators. If LA stays out of the box, its edge in possession against a 45% CF % team should show up. If it doesn't, Nashville's goaltending makes comebacks hard.

keyMatchups.title: Panarin's line against hot goalies
keyMatchups.body: The Islanders give up 28.2 shots a game and generate just 25.4, so LA should spend much of the night in their end. The obstacle is a goaltending group 4th in Goalies GSAx. LA's top line has to turn volume into goals against a .905 save %.

keyMatchups.title: Calgary's record outruns its play
keyMatchups.body: Calgary is 28th in Goal Diff / GP and 29th in shooting %, yet its Pts vs Goal Diff is 2.5 (2nd). Its defense also lets centers outproduce their norms, ranking 24th. This is the game where LA's better underlying play should translate into points.

weekAhead.watch: How many power-play goals LA concedes to Nashville and Calgary. The kill, not the even-strength game, decides whether this is a winning week.

restOfSeason.body:
The 66-point pace is too pessimistic. A 62.5% penalty kill, an .878 starter and a -2.5 Pts vs Goal Diff are all at the extreme end and should drift back. A near-50% xGF team with a top-12 power play usually plays around .500 hockey, and the last 10 games already look like that. I'd expect something like 70 to 82 points, with the kill climbing into the mid-to-high 70s.

What probably doesn't come back is the 2024-25 version of this team. The share of chances has fallen for three straight seasons, and the depth forwards and the center matchup look like lasting problems, not variance. Digging out of a 12-point start in a division where Edmonton and Vegas are already pulling away makes the playoffs a long shot rather than an expectation. A real goaltending recovery is the one path to the wild-card race.

projections.stat: Goal Diff / GP rest of season

swingFactors: Whether Kuemper recovers or Forsberg takes more starts
How far the penalty kill climbs from 62.5%
Depth forwards holding their own at 5-on-5

confidence.note: Only 15 games, and special-teams and save percentages are noisy, but the 5-on-5 shares and three seasons of history point the same way.
